true_positives.matched_candidate: Stored XSS: embed URL interpolated unescaped into imported post HTML `TopicEmbed.import` appends `#{url}` to the article contents with no HTML/attribute escaping, and the result is stored as a `raw_html` post (rendered verbatim via `raw post.cooked` and in the normal topic view). true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Stray `if` after `end` makes the next ERB statement the modifier condition

`<%- end if %>` compiles to Ruby `end if` followed by a newline, which Ruby parses as a modifier-`if` whose condition is the next generated statement (`@output_buffer.safe_append='...'`). It only works by accident because the buffer append returns a truthy string; the whitespace is emitted before the header button, and any future change to the following line (e.g. inserting another `<% %>` tag) would silently change behaviour or become a syntax error. This is not caught by the controller spec because rspec-rails does not render views by default. It should be `<%- end %>`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed items without <content:encoded> crash the poller and abort all remaining items

`i.content` is only populated for Atom `<content>` or RSS `<content:encoded>`; a plain RSS 2.0 feed that uses `<description>` (the common case) yields `nil`, so `nil.scrub` raises `NoMethodError`. Because the loop has no per-item error handling and the job is declared `sidekiq_options retry: false`, a single bad item (nil content, a link that fails `URI()` parsing in `absolutize_urls`, a `RecordNotUnique` race with the retrieve job, etc.) aborts the entire hourly import and all subsequent items are skipped. Fall back to `i.description`, and wrap each item in a rescue that logs and continues. Note also that `String#scrub` only exists in Ruby >= 2.1; if the project still supports 1.9.3/2.0 (the Gemfile still has 1.9-specific comments) this line raises `NoMethodError` everywhere.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
"requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" specs are vacuous; poll_feed itself is untested

These two examples do not stub `feed_polling_enabled?`, which defaults to `false`, so `poll_feed` is never reached regardless of the url/username settings; the tests would pass even if those guards were deleted. Each should stub the other two conditions to true and only the one under test to blank. In addition, `poll_feed` (the RSS parsing, `link`/`id` fallback, content unescaping, per-item import) has no coverage at all, which is how the nil `i.content` crash slipped through.

Already-shipped migration modified to add `force: true`, which drops the existing table

`20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` predates this PR and has already run on deployed databases; editing it to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` changes a committed migration and makes any re-run (e.g. `db:migrate:redo`, re-applying on a DB where the version row was lost) silently `DROP TABLE top_topics` and all its data. The new `create_topic_embeds` migration uses `force: true` too. If the intent is to work around a stale dev DB, that should be done locally rather than baked into migrations.

Anonymous users can trigger unbounded topic creation for arbitrary URLs on the embeddable host

Any request to `/embed/best` with an `embed_url` whose host matches `embeddable_host` enqueues a `retrieve_topic` job that fetches the URL and creates a topic authored by `embed_by_username`. The only protections are a Referer header check (freely forgeable by non-browser clients) and a 60-second per-URL Redis throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`. Because `embed_url` is stored verbatim (no normalisation), an attacker can vary the query string (`?a=1`, `?a=2`, ...) to mint an unlimited number of distinct URLs that all resolve to a 200 on a static blog, each producing a new topic and an outbound HTTP fetch, with no global rate limit. Additionally, every miss runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously (lib/topic_retriever.rb:41), so each probe also re-fetches and re-imports the whole RSS feed. Consider normalising URLs (strip query/fragment), only importing URLs that appear in the feed or match a path whitelist, and adding a global rate limit.

Disqus import now depends on a live HTTP fetch per thread; one failure aborts the whole import

The importer previously created the topic locally from the XML (`PostCreator` with the thread title, permalink and original `created_at`); it now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `open(url).read`. Old Disqus thread links frequently 404 or redirect, and `OpenURI::HTTPError`/timeouts are not rescued, so a single dead link aborts the entire run (the `ensure` block then restores settings). The `--category` option was also removed and the original thread `created_at` is no longer preserved on the topic, both silent behaviour regressions for existing users of the task.

New top-level assets (embed.css, embed.js) are not registered for precompilation

The layout references `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` and third-party sites are expected to load `embed.js` directly from Discourse's asset host, but the PR adds no change to `config.assets.precompile` (config/application.rb is not in the diff). In Rails 4 production, assets outside the manifest/precompile list are not compiled and either 404 or raise an asset-filtered error, so the embed would render unstyled and the blog-side `embed.js` would be unavailable. `embed.css` and `embed.js` need to be added to the precompile list (unless they are already there).

Only the Rails 4 lockfile was updated for the new gems

`ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` were added to the Gemfile and `Gemfile_rails4.lock`, but the Rails 3 lockfile (`Gemfile.lock`, used when `RAILS3` is set per the dual-boot logic at the top of the Gemfile) is not part of the change. If that lockfile is tracked, a Rails 3 boot with `bundle install --deployment`/frozen will fail because the Gemfile no longer matches the lock.

RSS feed content is stored and rendered as unsanitized raw HTML

`poll_feed` passes `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)` straight into `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates a post with `cook_method: raw_html`; `Post#cook` (app/models/post.rb:133) then returns `raw` untouched, so nothing in the pipeline strips `<script>`, event handlers or `javascript:` hrefs. The HTTP path at least runs Readability with a tag whitelist, but the RSS path has no sanitization at all, so any script in the feed (including syndicated user content or a compromised feed) becomes persistent XSS on the forum and inside the embed iframe. Even the Readability whitelist allows `href`/`src` values without scheme checks. Imported HTML should be run through the existing sanitizer (e.g. `Sanitize`/`PrettyText` whitelist) before being stored.

`skip_validations: true` only disables model validations; `RateLimiter::OnCreateRecord` hooks (`rate_limit` on `Post` and `Topic`) still run in `after_create` and raise `RateLimiter::LimitExceeded`. Unless `embed_by_username` is a staff account, importing more than one new topic within `rate_limit_create_topic` seconds (default 5) in the `poll_feed` loop, or more than `max_topics_per_day` (default 20) in a day, raises and aborts the job. The Disqus thor task explicitly calls `RateLimiter.disable` for exactly this reason, but `PollFeed`/`TopicRetriever` do not. Either disable the limiter around the import or document that the embed user must be staff.

`params.require(:embed_url)` raises `ActionController::ParameterMissing`, which Rails maps to 400 Bad Request, not 404; the example only asserts `should_not be_success` so the title is misleading. More importantly none of the examples use `render_views`, so `best.html.erb` and `loading.html.erb` (including the `end if` typo and `@topic_view.topic.url`/`small_avatar_url` calls) are never executed by the suite.

`post.present?` is true even when PostCreator failed, leading to NOT NULL violation

`PostCreator#create` returns the `Post` object even when creation was rolled back (e.g. `rollback_if_host_spam_detected` fires for a non-basic-trust embed user whose article links the same host several times, or the save fails); the object is unsaved with `id == nil`. `post.present?` is true for any AR object, so `TopicEmbed.create!` is called with `post_id: nil` and `topic_id` of an uncommitted topic, hitting the `null: false` constraints and raising `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` instead of returning nil. Worse, PostCreator raises `ActiveRecord::Rollback` inside its own `Post.transaction`, which is nested (without `requires_new`) inside the `Topic.transaction` here, so that Rollback is silently swallowed and does not roll back the already-created Topic until the later exception does. Check `post.persisted?`/`post.errors.empty?` instead.

absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs

`href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png` (very common in blog/RSS HTML), and `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, producing `http://embeddable-host/cdn.example.com/img.png`, a broken link/image. The same applies to `img[src]` at line 70. Check `start_with?('//')` first and only prepend the scheme, or use `URI.join(url, href)` which handles relative, root-relative and protocol-relative references correctly.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
align-items mixin emits a non-existent -ms property and omits the -moz legacy equivalent

`-ms-align-items` is not a property any IE version implemented (IE10 used `-ms-flex-align`, IE11 is unprefixed), so that line adds dead bytes to every rule that includes the mixin. Conversely, the `flexbox()` mixin emits `display: -moz-box` and the `order()` mixin emits `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, but `align-items()` has no `-moz-box-align`, so Firefox versions that fall into the `-moz-box` path get the ordering but never the alignment (they stay at the legacy default `stretch`). Either drop the `-moz-box` fallbacks consistently from all mixins or add `-moz-box-align` and remove `-ms-align-items`.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

false_positives.candidate:
.panel can be squeezed by long header content because it is a shrinkable flex item

`.d-header .contents` is now a flex container and `.panel` (the icons/login area) was changed from `float: right` to a flex item with `margin-left: auto` and `order: 3`. Floated blocks got a shrink-to-fit (max-content) width and never wrapped internally; a flex item defaults to `flex: 0 1 auto`, so when sibling content is wide the browser shrinks every item proportionally to its flex-basis. The `.extra-info-wrapper` sibling (order 2) carries the topic title, which can be hundreds of characters, so on topic pages with a long title the total max-content width exceeds the `.wrap` width and `.panel` loses a share of the overflow. `.panel`'s min-content width is only about one floated `li`/button wide, so its `.icons` and login/sign-up buttons wrap onto additional lines and the header grows taller. The icon panel needs `flex-shrink: 0` (or an explicit `flex: 0 0 auto`) so that only the title area absorbs the overflow, as it effectively did under the float layout.

Float fallbacks removed, so browsers without flexbox now get a vertically stacked header

The commit deletes `.title { float: left; }` and `.panel { float: right; }` while adding the flex mixins. `float` is ignored on flex items, so keeping those declarations would have cost nothing in flex-capable browsers but would have preserved the horizontal logo-left/icons-right layout as a fallback in engines that ignore every `display: *flex*` value (IE9 and earlier, Opera Mini, older Android stock browsers in some modes). After this change those browsers render `.title`, `.extra-info-wrapper` and `.panel` as stacked full-width blocks. If those browsers are still in the support matrix, the float declarations should be retained alongside the mixin includes.

PR title claims a performance optimization that the change does not make

The PR is titled "Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins" and its description is just "Test 5". The diff replaces float-based positioning with flexbox and adds vendor-prefixed mixins; nothing in it targets layout or paint performance, and flexbox layout is not generally cheaper than floats. Anyone reading the history will be misled about why the header, small-action posts and category badges changed appearance. The title/description should describe the actual change (migrate header and small-action layout to flexbox, add prefixed flex mixins) and note the visual adjustments to `.small-action-desc` spacing and `.extra-info-wrapper`.

align-items mixin passes modern keywords straight into legacy prefixed properties

`@mixin align-items($alignment)` writes the same `$alignment` value to `-webkit-box-align` (2009 box syntax) and `-ms-flex-align` (IE10 syntax). Those legacy properties accept `start`/`end`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`, so any caller using `align-items(flex-start)` or `align-items(flex-end)` will emit invalid declarations that old WebKit and IE10 silently drop, leaving the default `stretch` alignment there while modern browsers behave as requested. The current call sites only use `center` and `baseline` (valid in all syntaxes), but this is a shared mixin introduced for general use and should map `flex-start`→`start` and `flex-end`→`end` for the prefixed outputs, as the standard flexbox-mixin snippets do.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Injected placeholder refresh_token overwrites the real refresh token stored in the DB

When the parsed response lacks `refresh_token`, the function sets `data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. Callers then merge this into the stored credential: Zoom does `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token` and Office365 does `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`. In sync mode (where the self-hoster is told to return only access token and expiry) this replaces the user's real refresh token in Cal.com's DB with the literal string `"refresh_token"`, so if syncing is later disabled or the endpoint is unavailable the credential is permanently unusable without reconnecting. In non-sync mode Office365's `refresh_token` is optional in `refreshTokenResponseSchema`, so a response without it would also destroy the stored token (previously the spread simply left the existing value untouched). Do not fabricate a refresh token; leave the field absent so callers keep the existing value.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys evaluate to "[object Object]" and strip every field except access_token

`[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` do not create wildcard keys; `ZodType` has no custom `toString`, so both evaluate to the literal key `"[object Object]"` (the second overwriting the first). The resulting schema is effectively `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() })`, and because `z.object` strips unknown keys, in sync mode `data` contains only `access_token` (plus the injected placeholder `refresh_token`). Consequences: Zoom computes `key.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)` = NaN which is persisted as `null` and makes `zoomTokenSchema.parse(credential.key)` fail on the next call; Office365 never gets a new `expires_in` so it refreshes on every request; Salesforce loses `instance_url`/`id`/`signature` from the stored key so the next connection has `instanceUrl: undefined`. Use `.passthrough()`/`.catchall(z.unknown())` and explicitly handle expiry rather than computed keys.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google credential key is overwritten with a zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper object

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full zod safeParse result (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), not the parsed token. In `refreshAccessToken` the return value is assigned to `key` and written directly with `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. Previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` returned the token object itself. After the first token refresh, every Google Calendar credential in the DB becomes `{success: true, data: {...}}`; the next `GoogleCalendarService` construction calls `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` which throws, breaking Google Calendar (and Google Meet) for the user until they reconnect. This happens in all modes, not just when credential syncing is enabled. The callers in office365/zoom/salesforce correctly use `.data`; Google must do the same (`key: parsed.data`).

No tests for the new webhook or the shared refresh/parse utilities

The PR adds a new public API route and two shared OAuth utilities used by ~10 integrations, and modifies the token-refresh path of every OAuth app, but ships no tests (the checklist explicitly says none were added). Even a minimal unit test of `parseRefreshTokenResponse` would have caught that the computed-key schema strips all fields, and an integration test of the Google refresh path would have caught the SafeParseReturnType being stored as the credential key. The POST to the self-hoster's credential sync endpoint sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` as form fields with no secret, signature or bearer token. The inbound webhook already has `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`/`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`; the outbound call should at minimum send the same secret header so the endpoint can authenticate Cal.com.

When the parent application pushes fresh keys via this webhook, the update only sets `key`, so a previously invalidated credential stays flagged invalid and the UI/booking flows continue to treat it as broken even though it now has working tokens. `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` and then, if `count < deviceLimit`, performs an upsert in a separate session. Two or more first-time devices arriving concurrently (very likely with several Grafana replicas, since the per-instance `localCache` provides no cross-instance dedup) will all observe `count < limit` and all insert, so the stored device count can overshoot `device_limit`. If the limit is meant as a hard cap (e.g. for licensing/abuse control) this needs to be done in a single transaction with appropriate locking or a conditional insert; otherwise the setting should be documented as a soft limit. In practice the frontend fires many requests per page load, so at most the first one or two requests from an over-limit device get a 401 and the rest succeed — the configured `device_limit` is effectively not enforced. The bean now takes the first recovery-codes credential returned by `CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials()` (via `getFederatedCredentialsStream()`) and feeds it to `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel()`, which `JsonSerialization.readValue`s `credentialData` and `secretData` into `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialData`/`RecoveryAuthnCodesSecretData`, then calls `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get()`. `getCredentials()` was introduced so providers can list their credentials in the account console; nothing in that contract requires the model to carry Keycloak's internal hashed-code JSON. A provider that returns a `CredentialModel` with only id/type/label (or with its own data format) will now cause a NullPointerException/JSON parse exception while rendering the recovery-code login page, i.e. an HTTP 500 for every user of that provider who reaches the recovery-code step, where previously only local credentials were consulted. The new format requirement is also undocumented. Either guard the federated branch (fall back to code #1 / handle parse failures) or document that providers must return a model built with `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues`.

Storing new codes in user storage leaves a previously stored local recovery-codes credential intact and still valid

Before this change, recovery codes for federated users were always written via `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential`, which replaces the existing local credential of that type. Now, when `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` returns true (user storage took the codes), the local credential provider is never invoked, so any recovery-codes credential already stored in Keycloak's own store for that user (e.g. created before the storage provider added support for this type, or before upgrading) is left untouched. `SubjectCredentialManager.isValid()` validates against the user storage first and then falls through to the local `CredentialInputValidator`s, so the old local codes keep authenticating the user even though they believe they regenerated them, while the login form (`RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential`) only shows the state of the federated credential. When the user storage path succeeds, existing local credentials of type `recovery-authn-codes` should be removed as well.

User storage only receives raw codes; userLabel and generatedAt from the credential model are dropped and the payload format is undocumented

`createRecoveryCodesCredential` hands the user storage a `UserCredentialModel("", type, <JSON array of raw codes>)`. The `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` built in `RecoveryAuthnCodesAction.processAction` (which carries the user-supplied label and the `generatedAt` timestamp) is only used on the local-DB branch, so a storage provider has no way to learn the label or creation time the user set (the test provider ends up with a `null` label). The shape of the challenge-response string (a JSON list of 12-char raw codes with dashes removed) is also not stated anywhere in the Javadoc, so implementers of `CredentialInputUpdater.updateCredential` for this type have to reverse-engineer it. Document the payload format and consider passing label/createdDate (e.g. via `UserCredentialModel` notes) so the storage can persist them.

getCredentials() dereferences getMyUser(user) without null check

Every other credential method in this provider (`getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`, `isConfiguredFor`, `isValid`) guards against `getMyUser(user)` returning `null`, but the new `getCredentials` override immediately accesses `myUser.recoveryCodes` and `myUser.otp`. If the credential list is requested for a user that is no longer present in the in-memory map (e.g. account/admin listing after the user was removed from the storage but a stale `UserModel` is still being used), this throws a NullPointerException instead of returning an empty stream, and since `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` is now called from the login form bean and the recovery-code authenticator, the NPE would surface as a 500 during login rather than a graceful fallback.

Recovery codes stored in the test user storage can never be disabled/removed

The provider now stores recovery codes and reports them via `isConfiguredFor`/`getCredentials`, but `disableCredentialType` only handles OTP and `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` never lists `recovery-authn-codes`. Consequently admin `disableCredentialType`, the account-console delete path (which falls back to `disableCredentialType` for federated credentials), and the exhausted-codes handling in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` have no way to clear recovery codes held in this storage, and the new tests cannot (and do not) cover removal of recovery codes from user storage, unlike the existing OTP tests (`testOTPSetupThroughAdminRESTAndLogin`, `testDisableCredentialsInUserStorage`). Add recovery codes to both methods and a test that disables them.

Overriding getCredentials() for OTP (plus generating an OTP id) changes what the existing OTP backwards-compatibility test exercises

This class is documented as a frozen 4.8.3-era provider used to prove old providers keep working. The PR adds `newOTP.setId(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId())` and makes the new `getCredentials()` override return the OTP credential as well. `getCredentials()` is a defaulted method that an old provider would not implement, so after this change `testOTPSetupAndRemoveThroughAccountMgmtAndLogin` no longer exercises the legacy path where the account REST synthesizes the `otp-id` dummy credential (`CredentialHelper.createUserStorageCredentialRepresentation`) and deletes it via the `-id` suffix branch; it now goes through the real federated-credential listing instead. That legacy path loses its only coverage. Keep the OTP behaviour of the provider unchanged (return only recovery codes from `getCredentials`, or add a separate provider for the new feature) so both paths remain tested.

New test only covers the happy path of the user-storage branch

`testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` sets up codes once and logs in once with code #0. It does not cover: (a) a federated user whose storage provider does not support `recovery-authn-codes`, which is the new fallback branch in `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential` that must still create the credential in the local DB (previously the only behaviour for federated users); (b) a second login to show which code number the form requests after one has been consumed, or an invalid code being rejected by the storage; (c) that regenerating codes replaces the previous set. Because the test provider's `isValid` accepts any stored code and `getCredentials` rebuilds a fresh model each time, the sequential/consumed-code semantics of the authenticator are effectively untested for the user-storage path. At minimum add a fallback-to-local test for a federated user and an invalid-code assertion.

true_positives.golden_comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
V2 canManage() is granted by the VIEW scope on all groups

GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller has either VIEW or MANAGE on the Groups resource-type resource (`hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`). canManage() is what GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() checks via auth.groups().requireManage(), so an admin who was only granted the `view` scope on all groups can create top-level groups in the realm. This is a privilege escalation; the check should only accept AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE (mirroring canManage(GroupModel) which correctly checks MANAGE only). The GroupPermissionEvaluator javadoc for canManage() ("Also if it has permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups") encodes the same mistake and should be corrected too. No test covers a VIEW-only all-groups permission attempting to create a group.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug in GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(): its fallback accepts VIEW or MANAGE, allowing VIEW-only users to obtain management/write access. The candidate adds a concrete group-creation consequence and related documentation concerns without changing the underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes/returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs

In V2 a per-group Resource is created with name == group id (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup/getOrCreateResource) and GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String groupId, ...) resolves it with resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() however calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) with the authz resource UUID and then adds groupResource.getId() to the result set. Consequences: (1) findByName with a resource UUID never matches, so the code always falls back to the all-groups resource, meaning per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions are never detected and an all-groups permission is reported for every iterated resource; (2) the returned set contains resource UUIDs, but callers (UsersResource.searchForUser/getUsersCount, BruteForceUsersResource) feed it into session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...) and getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds), which expect group IDs, so user search/count return nothing. Both places should use groupResource.getName() and skip the "Groups" placeholder resource itself. Note also that getOrCreateResource never calls setType(resourceType) on the per-group resource, so findByType(server, "Groups") currently only returns the placeholder resource created in init(), making this method effectively dead for real groups and leaving GET /users/count wrong for admins with only group-member permissions.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same core mismatch: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes and returns authorization resource IDs, while hasPermission resolves by resource name and downstream filters expect underlying group IDs. Its additional observations do not change this semantic match.

false_positives.candidate:
Existence of any per-group permission disables the all-groups fallback for that group

hasPermission() only consults the Groups resource-type resource when no specific resource named by the group id exists. Once a specific resource exists for a group (e.g. because someone granted VIEW_MEMBERS on it), evaluation is done only against that resource and the requested scopes; if the specific permission does not include the requested scope (e.g. VIEW/MANAGE) the method returns false even though the caller holds an all-groups permission granting that scope. So granting a narrow per-group permission silently revokes broader type-level rights for that group (e.g. canView(group) becomes false for an admin with view-all-groups). The method should fall back to the type-level resource when the specific-resource evaluation does not grant the scope, or evaluate both.

requireManageMembers javadoc references the wrong predicate

The javadoc for requireManageMembers(GroupModel) says it throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false, but the implementations (GroupPermissions.requireManageMembers) check canManageMembers(GroupModel). The two scopes (manage-members vs manage-membership) have different meanings, so the doc misleads callers about which permission is enforced. Also, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission's @return says "Stream of IDs" while the method returns a Set.

No cleanup of V2 group resources/permissions when a group is removed

The ProviderEventListener that reacts to GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent is registered only when the V1 feature (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) is enabled, and even then it calls groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false), which GroupPermissionsV2 implements by throwing UnsupportedOperationException. With this PR, V2 now creates per-group authz Resources (named by group id) and scope permissions referencing them, but nothing removes them when the group is deleted. Deleted groups therefore leave orphaned Resource/Policy rows in the admin-permissions resource server that keep showing up in permission listings and in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()/findByType iterations.

getResourceName has no handling for the new Groups resource type

getResourceName() maps Users resources to a human-readable name ("All users" or the username) but falls through to resource.getDisplayName() for everything else. Group resources created by getOrCreateResource() have name == group id and no display name set, so for Groups-type permissions this returns null (and the "Groups" placeholder gets no "All groups" label). Any consumer that relies on this method (e.g. admin UI permission listings) will show empty names for group permissions. A Groups branch resolving the group and returning its name/path, plus an "All groups" label, is needed for parity with Users.

MANAGE_MEMBERS cannot be used to create users in V2 because canCreateGroupMembers is gated on the V1 feature flag

canCreateGroupMembers() returns false unless Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled. V1 and V2 are versions of the same feature and cannot be enabled together, so under ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 the newly added Groups MANAGE_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP scopes are never consulted when creating a user with `groups` in the representation; createUser() always fails with 403 unless the admin has the manage-users role or an all-users MANAGE permission. Either the gate should also accept V2 or the limitation should be documented.

Missing negative/edge coverage for new group scopes

The new test class only exercises happy paths for the Groups scopes. Not covered: (a) that an all-groups VIEW permission does NOT allow creating a top-level group (which would catch the canManage() VIEW bug); (b) that joining a group requires the group-level MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP permission (testManageGroupMembership grants both all-users MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP and the group permission at once, so a missing group check would not be detected); (c) GET /groups/{id}/members with VIEW_MEMBERS; (d) GET /users/count for an admin with only group VIEW_MEMBERS permissions (which exercises getGroupIdsWithViewPermission and would expose the resource-id vs group-id bug); (e) a group with a specific narrow permission plus an all-groups VIEW permission (fallback behaviour).

Per-subgroup policy evaluation before pagination in V2

getSubGroups() loads all subgroups (getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, -1, -1)) and filters with auth.groups()::canView before paginating. In V2, canView(GroupModel) does not short-circuit on a global permission: each call does a resource lookup, a policyStore.findByResource on the type resource and a full policy evaluation. For an admin with an all-groups VIEW permission on a parent with thousands of children this results in thousands of policy evaluations per page request (same pattern in GroupsResource.getGroups). The previous code evaluated the global check once (canViewGlobal); if per-group negative permissions must be honoured, consider at least caching the all-groups evaluation result within the evaluator instance for the request.

No regression test asserting SQL expressions are rejected even with the feature flag enabled

true_positives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Count-then-insert limit check is not atomic; concurrent new devices can exceed the limit

`CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` and then, if `count < deviceLimit`, performs an upsert in a separate session. Two or more first-time devices arriving concurrently (very likely with several Grafana replicas, since the per-instance `localCache` provides no cross-instance dedup) will all observe `count < limit` and all insert, so the stored device count can overshoot `device_limit`. If the limit is meant as a hard cap (e.g. for licensing/abuse control) this needs to be done in a single transaction with appropriate locking or a conditional insert; otherwise the setting should be documented as a soft limit. Additionally the `COUNT(*)` runs on every cache miss even when the device already exists and will simply be updated, which is an avoidable extra query on the request path.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same race condition: concurrent requests can pass the non-atomic device count check and insert devices beyond the limit. Both recommend transactions or locking to enforce the cap.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Local cache is populated before the limit check, so a rejected device bypasses the limit on its next request

`tagDeviceUI` writes the device key into `localCache` (29‑minute TTL) *before* calling `anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`. With this PR, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` can now fail with `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, and `Anonymous.Authenticate` turns that into an authentication failure. But because the cache entry was already set, every subsequent request from the same device within the next 29 minutes hits the cache early-return (`return nil`) in `tagDeviceUI`, `TagDevice` reports success, and `Authenticate` issues a normal anonymous identity. In practice the frontend fires many requests per page load, so at most the first one or two requests from an over-limit device get a 401 and the rest succeed — the configured `device_limit` is effectively not enforced. The cache must only be populated after the store call succeeds (and a rejection should not be cached, or should be cached as a negative result that keeps rejecting).
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: tagDeviceUI caches the device before CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds, leaving the cache entry intact after ErrDeviceLimitReached and allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit for the 29-minute TTL.

false_positives.candidate:
Device limit is only applied to requests carrying X-Grafana-Device-Id; omitting the header bypasses it entirely

`TagDevice` returns `nil` immediately when the `X-Grafana-Device-Id` header is absent, and `Anonymous.Authenticate` then issues a full anonymous identity. The header is set voluntarily by the Grafana frontend JS; any client that strips it (curl, scripts, a modified browser) is never counted and never limited, so `auth.anonymous.device_limit` is trivially circumvented and cannot be relied on as an access control. If the limit is intended to be enforceable, requests without a device id should be rejected (or at least documented as uncounted) when a limit is configured.

Limit tests only cover rejection of a new device; no coverage for existing-device updates or the service/client enforcement path

`TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only asserts that a second, new device is rejected when `deviceLimit=1`. There is no test that an already-registered active device can still be updated once the limit is reached (the `updateDevice` success path and its `updated_at BETWEEN` window), no test that a stale device (older than 30 days) is treated as new, and no test at the `AnonDeviceService`/`Anonymous.Authenticate` level that a limit-exceeding device actually fails authentication on repeated requests. The last gap is exactly what hides the local-cache bypass bug in `tagDeviceUI`; a test issuing two `TagDevice`/`Authenticate` calls for the same over-limit device would have caught it.

Limit-reached failure surfaces as a generic 401 and warning-level log noise

`Authenticate` returns the raw `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached` (a plain `fmt.Errorf`). The authn service joins it into the generic auth error, logs a `Warn` for every request, and middleware responds with a bare 401 'Unauthorized'; the frontend cannot distinguish 'device limit reached' from any other auth failure, so the newly exposed `anonymousDeviceLimit` setting cannot be used to show a meaningful message. The error is also logged at Debug in `TagDevice`, then re-logged upstream. Consider an `errutil` error with a public message/status so the UI can present the condition, and log at a lower level since this is expected behaviour under load.

anonymousDeviceLimit is typed as `undefined` in the runtime config and the backend always sends a number

`anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` with no type annotation gives the class property the literal type `undefined`, so `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` in `@grafana/runtime` is unusable for numeric comparisons without a cast (any `config.anonymousDeviceLimit > 0` is a compile error). Meanwhile `FrontendSettingsDTO.AnonymousDeviceLimit` is a non-omitempty `int64`, so the backend always serialises a number (0 when unset); the `number | undefined` type in `packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts` is therefore misleading as well. Declare it as `anonymousDeviceLimit = 0` (or `: number`) to match the wire format.

New `device_limit` setting is not added to defaults.ini/sample.ini or configuration docs

`cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit` is read from `[auth.anonymous] device_limit`, but the PR does not add the key to `conf/defaults.ini`, `conf/sample.ini`, or the configuration documentation, and the PR description leaves the why/who sections unfilled. Operators have no discoverable way to learn the setting exists, its default (0 = unlimited), or its semantics (30-day active-device window, soft limit, only applies to requests with a device id). Grafana convention is for every new ini key to appear in both ini files with a comment and in the configure-grafana docs.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
align-items mixin emits a non-existent -ms property and omits the -moz legacy equivalent

`-ms-align-items` is not a property any IE version implemented (IE10 used `-ms-flex-align`, IE11 is unprefixed), so that line adds dead bytes to every rule that includes the mixin. false_positives.candidate:
`prisma` used without being imported in Salesforce CalendarService

The new refresh-and-persist logic calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` but the file never imports `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma` (the import list only has jsforce, rrule, zod, lib helpers, types, `getAppKeysFromSlug` and `parseRefreshTokenResponse`). This is a TypeScript error and, if it ever ran, a `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` on every Salesforce service instantiation, making the Salesforce integration unusable. Add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";`.

appStoreMetadata is keyed by app directory name, not slug, so the webhook 404s for most apps

`appStoreMetadata` (from `apps.metadata.generated.ts`) is keyed by the app's directory name (`googlecalendar`, `office365calendar`, `zoomvideo`, `office365video`, `larkcalendar`, ...), not by `slug` (`google-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `zoom`, `msteams`, `lark-calendar`). The handler looks up `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` after confirming the slug exists in the `App` table, so for every app whose dirName differs from its slug the lookup is `undefined` and the request returns 404 "App not found. Ensure that you have the correct app slug" even though the slug is correct. Only apps where dirName === slug (hubspot, salesforce, zohocrm, webex, zoho-bigin) work. Use `getAppFromSlug(slug)` from `@calcom/app-store/utils` (which searches by `slug`) instead.

Injected placeholder refresh_token overwrites the real refresh token stored in the DB

When the parsed response lacks `refresh_token`, the function sets `data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. Callers then merge this into the stored credential: Zoom does `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token` and Office365 does `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`. In sync mode (where the self-hoster is told to return only access token and expiry) this replaces the user's real refresh token in Cal.com's DB with the literal string `"refresh_token"`, so if syncing is later disabled or the endpoint is unavailable the credential is permanently unusable without reconnecting. In non-sync mode Office365's `refresh_token` is optional in `refreshTokenResponseSchema`, so a response without it would also destroy the stored token (previously the spread simply left the existing value untouched). Do not fabricate a refresh token; leave the field absent so callers keep the existing value.

Request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication

The POST to the self-hoster's credential sync endpoint sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` as form fields with no secret, signature or bearer token. The endpoint must return live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary users, so unless the self-hoster adds out-of-band protection (network allowlisting), anyone who discovers the URL can obtain any user's third-party access tokens by posting a user id. The inbound webhook already has `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`/`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`; the outbound call should at minimum send the same secret header so the endpoint can authenticate Cal.com.

Sync request uses "zoomvideo" while the webhook requires the DB slug "zoom"

The `appSlug` sent to the credential sync endpoint for Zoom is the directory name `"zoomvideo"`, but the inbound `/api/webhook/app-credential` endpoint validates `appSlug` against `App.slug` in the DB, which is `"zoom"`. Other apps send their real slug (`google-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `msteams`, `lark-calendar`). Self-hosters implementing the sync endpoint will have to special-case Zoom. Use `"zoom"` for consistency.

Webex and Lark refresh paths route through the sync endpoint but keep provider-specific strict response validation

Webex now calls `refreshOAuthTokens` (so in sync mode the response comes from the self-hoster) but still validates with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires `scope` to be the exact literal `"spark:kms meeting:schedules_read meeting:schedules_write"`, `token_type: "Bearer"`, `refresh_token` and `refresh_token_expires_in`. Lark similarly passes the sync response through `handleLarkError`, which expects Lark's `{ code: 0, data: { access_token, refresh_token, expires_in, refresh_expires_in } }` envelope. The comment in `refreshOAuthTokens` tells self-hosters the response "should only contain the access token and expiry date", so a conforming endpoint will be rejected by both apps. Either use `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (once fixed) in these apps or document the full provider-shaped response they require.

Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==` and no method restriction

The shared secret is checked with a plain string inequality, which is vulnerable in principle to timing side channels; use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers (as other webhook handlers in the repo do for signatures). The handler also accepts any HTTP method (GET included) and will read `req.body`; it should reject non-POST requests with 405.

Updating an existing credential does not clear the `invalid` flag

Google Calendar and Zoom/Webex mark a credential `invalid: true` when the provider returns `invalid_grant`. When the parent application pushes fresh keys via this webhook, the update only sets `key`, so a previously invalidated credential stays flagged invalid and the UI/booking flows continue to treat it as broken even though it now has working tokens. The update should also set `invalid: false`.

No tests for the new webhook or the shared refresh/parse utilities

The PR adds a new public API route and two shared OAuth utilities used by ~10 integrations, and modifies the token-refresh path of every OAuth app, but ships no tests (the checklist explicitly says none were added). Even a minimal unit test of `parseRefreshTokenResponse` would have caught that the computed-key schema strips all fields, and an integration test of the Google refresh path would have caught the SafeParseReturnType being stored as the credential key. Please add unit tests for `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, `refreshOAuthTokens` (both branches), and the webhook handler (auth failure, unknown slug, create vs update).
